supporting_sources.exact_english_quote: The input `height` lists vertical wall heights at positions `0, 1, ..., n - 1`. Choose two distinct positions `i < j`; the ground and those two walls form an upright container. Return the largest capacity, as an integer, rather than the wall positions. The statement allows `2 <= n <= 100000` and `0 <= height[i] <= 10000`. It does not ask us to change the input, and the solutions below leave it unchanged. Empty and one-wall inputs are outside this contract. [LeetCode problem statement](https://leetcode.com/problems/container-with-most-water/).

Suppose `height[left] <= height[right]`. The pair just measured has area `(right - left) * height[left]`. Consider any pair that keeps `left` and replaces `right` with an inner position `k`. Its width `k - left` is smaller, and its water height cannot exceed `height[left]`, even if the new wall is much taller. Because heights are nonnegative,
`area(left, k) <= (k - left) * height[left] <= (right - left) * height[left]`.

When the right wall is shorter, the same argument applies with the sides reversed: keeping `right` while moving the left endpoint inward cannot improve the area just measured, so decrease `right`. If the heights are equal, either endpoint may be discarded by the same inequality. The code chooses to discard the left one. Zero-height ties remain safe because every pair keeping either zero-height wall has area zero.

supporting_sources.exact_english_quote: Suppose `height[left] <= height[right]`. The pair just measured has area `(right - left) * height[left]`. Consider any pair that keeps `left` and replaces `right` with an inner position `k`. Its width `k - left` is smaller, and its water height cannot exceed `height[left]`, even if the new wall is much taller. Because heights are nonnegative,

So no such pair can beat the endpoint area we already recorded. Every remaining candidate involving `left` can be discarded together by increasing `left` by one. This is a bound on all its possible partners, not a prediction that the next wall is taller or that the next area will improve.

checkpoint.text: 先計算當前兩端面積並更新 best，才移動 endpoint。完成這次 iteration、再次檢查 while 條件時，所有區間外配對才由更新後的 best 涵蓋；不可把尚未記錄的當前配對省略。

supporting_sources.exact_english_quote: The area formula describes one pair. Correctness of the whole search needs a separate loop invariant, a statement that remains true at a chosen checkpoint. At the start of every `while` condition check: `best` is the maximum area among pairs already evaluated, or zero if none were evaluated; every pair with an endpoint outside the current interval has area at most `best`.

During an iteration, measuring the endpoints and updating `best` preserves the first claim. The discard inequality proves that every newly excluded pair has area at most the area just measured, which is at most the updated `best`. Previously excluded pairs remain covered because `best` never decreases. These facts reestablish the invariant for either branch, including equal heights.

annotations.original_zh_tw: 對 termination 而言，最多只能移除 `numCourses` 門互不相同的課程。如果全部都被移除，這些合法步驟便構成 schedule。否則，queue 已空，但仍有課未完成。依 checkpoint，每門這樣的課都還有一門未完成的 prerequisite。前面的有限集合往回追蹤論證因此會找到 cycle，所以不可能存在完整 schedule。最後的比較因而涵蓋兩種結果。這個 algorithm 常稱為 Kahn's topological sort；topological order 會把每門 prerequisite 排在其 dependent 前面。
annotations.original_english: For termination, at most `numCourses` distinct courses can be removed. If all were removed, those legal steps establish a schedule. Otherwise the queue is empty with some courses unfinished. The checkpoint says each such course still has an unfinished prerequisite. The finite backward-following argument above then finds a cycle, so no full schedule is possible. The final comparison therefore covers both results. This algorithm is often called Kahn's topological sort; a topological order places every prerequisite before its dependent.
annotations.explanation_zh_tw: 在整份 dependent list 更新完成、準備再次判斷 while ready 的 checkpoint，若所有課都已合法完成，就存在 schedule；若 queue 空且仍有未完成課，則每門剩餘課都在等另一門剩餘 prerequisite。有限 graph 中反覆往回追必重遇節點，因而有 cycle；處理途中 queue 暫時為空不能套用此結論。

premises.text: 對有限的課程集合，每個 [a, b] 表示 b 必須先於 a 完成。finished 計算互不相同的合法完成；queue 保存所有且僅有目前可開始的未完成課程，恰各一次。這使 finished == numCourses 能代表全部合法完成。

supporting_sources.exact_english_quote: In [LeetCode 207](https://leetcode.com/problems/course-schedule/), course identifiers run from `0` through `numCourses - 1`. A pair `[a, b]` means that `b` must be finished before `a`. Return a Boolean indicating whether every course can be finished. A schedule itself is not required. There are 1 to 2000 courses and 0 to 5000 distinct prerequisite pairs; both identifiers belong to the course range. The statement does not exclude `[a, a]`, which makes that course impossible to start. The implementation below leaves the input unchanged.

The checkpoint is just before each evaluation of `while ready`, after all updates for the preceding completion. At that point, `finished` counts distinct completed courses; every unfinished course's count equals its number of unfinished prerequisites; and the queue contains every available unfinished course exactly once. Completed courses are outside the queue. The queue's internal order is an implementation choice, separate from these conditions.

For maintenance, removing an available course is legal because all its prerequisites are completed. Its outgoing edges describe exactly the obligations that this completion satisfies. Decrementing those destinations updates the counts correctly, without changing any unrelated count. Each destination newly reaching zero enters once; other available courses remain queued. Increasing `finished` records this one new completion. The checkpoint holds again after the whole dependent list is processed, rather than midway through it.

For termination, at most `numCourses` distinct courses can be removed. If all were removed, those legal steps establish a schedule. Otherwise the queue is empty with some courses unfinished. The checkpoint says each such course still has an unfinished prerequisite. The finite backward-following argument above then finds a cycle, so no full schedule is possible. The final comparison therefore covers both results. This algorithm is often called Kahn's topological sort; a topological order places every prerequisite before its dependent.
